taxonomyNote: NatureServe places North American treefrogs in Dryophytes (Duellman et al. 2016); ADW and the batch list use Hyla. NatureServe name: Dryophytes gratiosus.
fieldMarks: Largest treefrog in the southeastern US: 5.1-7 cm, bulky.
Colour varies from bright lime green to brown but almost always with darker back spots.
Lighter stripe from the upper jaw along the body; males have a light green or yellow throat.
Rounded pads on the digits; loud 'bark' call.
behavior: Nocturnal; rests high in trees by day and is mostly arboreal.
Burrows under roots, vegetation or soil in cold or dry seasons.
Breeds after heavy rains in spring or summer; clutches up to about 2,000 eggs; groups generally under 20-25 males.
habitat: Sandy pine savannas and low wet woods and swamps; breeds in shallow ponds, swamps and bayheads, preferring semi-permanent ponds without fish.
range: Coastal Plain and some uplands from North Carolina to southern Florida and west to Louisiana, including northern Mississippi; disjunct populations in Delaware and Maryland, southwestern Kentucky and Tennessee and southeastern Virginia; introduced and probably extirpated in southern New Jersey. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Green treefrog
lookalikes.howToTell: Smooth skin and a bright white or yellowish side stripe; smaller.
